weapon_qualities.name: Ammunition
weapon_qualities.summary: As alternative ammunition, the attack uses the range of the weapon it is fired from based on that weapon's normal range due to its standard effect.
weapon_qualities.text: As alternative ammunition, the attack uses the range of the weapon it is fired from based on that weapon's normal range due to its standard effect. Do not use the range that would normally be associated with this particular effect's rank. +0 or +1 flat point per rank if the weapon the ammunition is fired from doubles or more the effect's normal range based on its rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Accurate
weapon_qualities.summary: Attacks with the weapon gain a +2 bonus to the attack check per rank of this quality.
weapon_qualities.text: Attacks with the weapon gain a +2 bonus to the attack check per rank of this quality. This bonus counts towards power level determinations. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Aura
weapon_qualities.summary: The striking portion of the weapon is surrounded by an aura of some damaging force or energy (not the same as the Energy Aura power from the core rules, however).
weapon_qualities.text: The striking portion of the weapon is surrounded by an aura of some damaging force or energy (not the same as the Energy Aura power from the core rules, however). In game terms, this applies an additional descriptor to the weapon's damage. For example, a sword with a flame aura has the "fire" descriptor while a hammer with a lightning aura has the "electrical" descriptor on its damage in addition to bludgeoning. This is primarily just a Damage descriptor but may, like the basic descriptors for damage type, change how the weapon affects some targets, such as a foe vulnerable to fire. The aura may also allow the wielder to perform different stunts with the weapon. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Bane
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is especially effective against a certain type of target.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is especially effective against a certain type of target. This is typically additional ranks of Damage with a Limited flaw based on how rarely the target appears. Excluding about half the potential targets is worth a -1 flaw. Since the benefits of Bane are limited by power level, they can make the weapon less effectual overall. As such, Gamemasters may wish to bend the power level limits for Bane weapons, allowing their additional Damage bonus to exceed power level limits by up to 2 ranks. More than this is not recommended. -1cost per rank .

weapon_qualities.name: Binding
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon grants the benefits of the Weapon Bind advantage.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon grants the benefits of the Weapon Bind advantage. If you take a defend action while wielding the weapon, and successfully defend against an armed attack, you can make an immediate disarm attempt against the attacker as a reaction. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Breaking
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon grants the benefits of the Weapon Break advantage.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon grants the benefits of the Weapon Break advantage. If you take a defend action while wielding the weapon, and successfully defend against an armed attack, you can make an immediate smash attack against the attacker's weapon as a reaction. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Carrier
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's attack and damage serve as a carrier for another Linked effect, such as Affliction or Weaken.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's attack and damage serve as a carrier for another Linked effect, such as Affliction or Weaken. The descriptor may be anything from a powerful electrical shock to a toxin or even a magical effect. The Linked effect may have its own modifiers to further define it. Linked effect cost.

weapon_qualities.name: Choking
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon provides the benefits of the Chokehold advantage.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon provides the benefits of the Chokehold advantage. After successful attack and grab checks, the target suffocates for as long as you maintain the hold. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Climbing
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is designed to help the wielder with climbing.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is designed to help the wielder with climbing. Each rank of this weapon quality provides a +2 bonus to Athletics checks for the purpose of climbing. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Concealable
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is small and easy to conceal or can fold or collapse down into a concealable form.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is small and easy to conceal or can fold or collapse down into a concealable form. This is similar to the Subtle modifier, and provides a +10 circumstance bonus to Sleight of Hand checks to conceal the weapon (base DC 20 to find it when it is concealed as a routine check). +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Dangerous
weapon_qualities.summary: Dangerous weapons are more likely to inflict critical hits.
weapon_qualities.text: Dangerous weapons are more likely to inflict critical hits. Each rank of this quality increases the weapon's critical threat range by 1, to a maximum of 16-20 with 4 ranks. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Defensive
weapon_qualities.summary: Like the Improved Defense advantage, when you take the defend action while wielding the weapon, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your active defense checks.
weapon_qualities.text: Like the Improved Defense advantage, when you take the defend action while wielding the weapon, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your active defense checks. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Disabling
weapon_qualities.summary: Disabling weapons are more likely to inflict disabling critical hits.
weapon_qualities.text: Disabling weapons are more likely to inflict disabling critical hits. Each rank of this quality increases the weapon's disabling threat range by 1, to a maximum of 16-20 with 4 ranks. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Disarming
weapon_qualities.summary: A disarming weapon is more effective in knocking things out of a target's grasp, allowing disarm attempts to be made with no circumstance penalty.
weapon_qualities.text: A disarming weapon is more effective in knocking things out of a target's grasp, allowing disarm attempts to be made with no circumstance penalty. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Double
weapon_qualities.summary: A double weapon has two striking ends or sides, and can be used to strike twice, splitting the weapon's damage (as per the Split extra).
weapon_qualities.text: A double weapon has two striking ends or sides, and can be used to strike twice, splitting the weapon's damage (as per the Split extra). +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Easy
weapon_qualities.summary: An easy weapon is so simple to use that the wielder can use it with their fighting style even if they do not have the appropriate Weapon Element.
weapon_qualities.text: An easy weapon is so simple to use that the wielder can use it with their fighting style even if they do not have the appropriate Weapon Element. However, a -1 penalty to initiative and attack is suffered while doing so. The Gamemaster may rule that some fighting styles cannot make use of this benefit if the types of attacks they use cannot utilize a weapon of that type at all. A fighting style that solely employs kicks, for example, would gain no such benefit with a cestus. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Empowered
weapon_qualities.summary: Because of its design, weight, etc., the weapon's successful critical hits enjoys the benefits of one rank of the Empowered Critical advantage.
weapon_qualities.text: Because of its design, weight, etc., the weapon's successful critical hits enjoys the benefits of one rank of the Empowered Critical advantage. A second rank of this weapon quality can be applied, as per the advantage. No further benefit is enjoyed if the total ranks of Empowered Critical from the wielder and weapon are greater than 2. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Entangling
weapon_qualities.summary: Grab attacks made with the weapon are particularly difficult to escape from.
weapon_qualities.text: Grab attacks made with the weapon are particularly difficult to escape from. Grabbed targets suffer a -2 circumstance penalty to checks to escape. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Extended
weapon_qualities.summary: Attacks made with this reach weapon are made with half the usual attack bonus if the target is closer than the weapon's maximum reach.
weapon_qualities.text: Attacks made with this reach weapon are made with half the usual attack bonus if the target is closer than the weapon's maximum reach. For 2 points, targets within such proximity cannot be effectively attacked at all with the weapon. -1 or -2 flat points per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Grabbing
weapon_qualities.cost: +1 flat point (no cost if the attack has no other effect)
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon provides the benefits of the Fast Grab advantage.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon provides the benefits of the Fast Grab advantage. After a hit with the weapon, make an immediate grab check against the target as a free action. Use the weapon's Damage rank as its effective Strength rank. The weapon attack inflicts its normal damage and counts as the initial attack check to grab the target. +1 flat point. No cost if the weapon attack has no effect other than the grab.

weapon_qualities.name: Impressive
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's design or function is sufficiently impressive to grant the wielder a +2 circumstance bonus to interaction checks involving it.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's design or function is sufficiently impressive to grant the wielder a +2 circumstance bonus to interaction checks involving it. This usually takes the form of Intimidation checks when using the weapon to threaten someone. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Inaccurate
weapon_qualities.summary: Attacks with the weapon suffer a -2 penalty to the attack check per rank of this quality.
weapon_qualities.text: Attacks with the weapon suffer a -2 penalty to the attack check per rank of this quality. -1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Indestructible
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's physical form cannot be damaged.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's physical form cannot be damaged. It is immune to smash attacks and, while it can be taken away from the wielder, it cannot be destroyed. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Knockabout
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's weight or design means it knocks the target about a bit more.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's weight or design means it knocks the target about a bit more. Each rank increases the weapon's Damage by +1, but only for the purpose of determining whether knockback occurs and for knockback distance. In this manner, it functions like the Enhanced Knockback * advantage. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Nonlethal
weapon_qualities.summary: Although most anything can kill, the weapon is intended to make this outcome much less likely.
weapon_qualities.text: Although most anything can kill, the weapon is intended to make this outcome much less likely. It is only capable of inflicting a dying or dead condition upon landing a critical hit or as a finishing attack. -1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Penetrating
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's Damage has the Penetrating modifier, allowing it to overcome Impervious Toughness, typically due to extreme sharpness or other "armor piercing" capability.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's Damage has the Penetrating modifier, allowing it to overcome Impervious Toughness, typically due to extreme sharpness or other "armor piercing" capability. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Personal
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is "keyed" to the wielder in some fashion (biometric signature, aura reading, magical link, etc.) such that only the intended wielder may use it.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is "keyed" to the wielder in some fashion (biometric signature, aura reading, magical link, etc.) such that only the intended wielder may use it. The weapon simply doesn't function for anyone else. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Ranged
weapon_qualities.cost: 0 points (the complication pays for the extra)
weapon_qualities.summary: Ranged use of exotic or archaic weapons is often handled by one of three methods: First Method The weapon is generally used at range and has the Ranged modifier on its Damage.
weapon_qualities.text: Ranged use of exotic or archaic weapons is often handled by one of three methods: First Method The weapon is generally used at range and has the Ranged modifier on its Damage. It may or may not be Strength-Based, and ammunition is handled as a complication if it becomes one. This suits weapons like bows and slings, as well as things like hammers or shields that return to the wielder's hand when thrown. +1 point per rank. Second Method The weapon is used at range, but has a very finite number of uses (5 or less). It has the Ranged modifier on its Damage, but is Unreliable. This suits things like a brace of throwing knives or shuriken that run out quickly. +0 points per rank. Third Method The weapon can be used at range (typically thrown), but doing so deprives the wielder of the weapon until it can be retrieved, such as throwing a hammer, spear, or similar weapon. This is best treated as a combination of a stunt (allowing the weapon to attack at range) and a complication (depriving the wielder of the weapon) when it happens, with no change in the weapon's point cost and no fatigue or hero point cost for the stunt. In essence, the complication "pays" for the one-time extra. 0 points.

weapon_qualities.name: Reach
weapon_qualities.cost: +1 flat point per +5 feet of reach
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's length or design provides the wielder with additional reach in attacking nearby targets.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's length or design provides the wielder with additional reach in attacking nearby targets. +1 flat point per +5 feet of reach.

weapon_qualities.name: Reinforced
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon's Toughness is considered double normal for the sake of how much Strength may be applied while wielding it before it will break.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon's Toughness is considered double normal for the sake of how much Strength may be applied while wielding it before it will break. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Reluctant
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is not easily disarmed, granting the wielder a +2 bonus per rank to resist a disarm attempt.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is not easily disarmed, granting the wielder a +2 bonus per rank to resist a disarm attempt. +1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Risky
weapon_qualities.summary: A critical miss with this weapon requires the wielder make an attack roll against themselves to see if they have inadvertently harmed themselves with the weapon.
weapon_qualities.text: A critical miss with this weapon requires the wielder make an attack roll against themselves to see if they have inadvertently harmed themselves with the weapon. -1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Short Throw
weapon_qualities.summary: The distance the weapon may be thrown is half normal.
weapon_qualities.text: The distance the weapon may be thrown is half normal. -1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Smashing
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is especially effective at smashing held objects.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is especially effective at smashing held objects. You suffer no attack check penalty for making a smash attack against an object held by another character. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Stylistic
weapon_qualities.summary: The weapon is designed specifically for the forms, grip, and other characteristics of a particular fighting style.
weapon_qualities.text: The weapon is designed specifically for the forms, grip, and other characteristics of a particular fighting style. This fighting style must be selected when this weapon quality is applied (essentially, when the weapon is made) and cannot be changed later. A wielder who practices this fighting style and has assumed any of its stances (excluding Neutral) gains a +1 bonus to attack and initiative with it while employing that fighting style's attacks. Anyone wielding the weapon and using a different fighting style or a Neutral stance suffers a -1 initiative penalty. +1 flat point.

weapon_qualities.name: Tricky
weapon_qualities.summary: The wielder's critical miss range with the weapon increases by one per rank of this weapon quality, as per the Uncertain flaw (pg 98).-1 flat point per rank.
weapon_qualities.text: The wielder's critical miss range with the weapon increases by one per rank of this weapon quality, as per the Uncertain flaw (pg 98).-1 flat point per rank.

weapon_qualities.name: Weak
weapon_qualities.summary: Only half (rounded down) of the wielder's Strength bonus applies to the Strength-Based weapon.
weapon_qualities.text: Only half (rounded down) of the wielder's Strength bonus applies to the Strength-Based weapon. Apply the full Strength penalty, if applicable. If halving the Strength bonus results in a modifier less than +1, no Strength bonus is applied. -1 flat point.

ma_weapons.name: Brass Knuckles
ma_weapons.description: Pieces of molded metal fitting over the fingers, brass knuckles add +1 damage to your unarmed strikes. They include similar items like chain-wrapped fists.

ma_weapons.name: Caltrop
ma_weapons.effect: Burst Area Affliction 6 (Resisted by Dodge; Hindered and Impaired), Continuous, Extra Condition, Limited Degree 2; Limited to Speed 0 or Faster or Fighting
ma_weapons.description: These are multi-pronged metal spikes designed so one prong points up when the caltrop rests on a surface. You can scatter caltrops on the ground to injure opponents or, at least, slow them down. One bag of caltrops covers up to a 30-foot radius area. Each time someone moves at a rate greater than Speed -1 (or without sufficient ability to sense the area) through an area with caltrops, or each round someone spends fighting in such an area, the caltrops may slow them down (painfully). ma_weapons.name: Cestus
ma_weapons.description: A glove or fist wrapping fitted with spikes and/or weights along its back and knuckles to enhance a punch's damage.

ma_weapons.name: Club
ma_weapons.description: The simplest bludgeoning weapon, possibly even a makeshift weapon, although clubs and cudgels (like the Irish shillelagh) suit some character concepts. Spikes may be added to a club, increasing Damage by +1 (piercing; +1 flat point).

ma_weapons.name: Fighting Stick
ma_weapons.description: Whether called a stick, baton, or a more cultural or specific martial term, this weapon represents all simple thin, long sticks held one-handed for the purpose of combat. Fighting sticks are often used for their (comparative) lack of lethality or as a substitute for swords.

ma_weapons.name: Gaff/Hook
ma_weapons.description: This metal hook is used by sailors to load and unload ships. Occasionally a prosthetic one is used to replace a severed hand.

ma_weapons.name: Kunai
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 1 (piercing), Climbing, Concealable, Dangerous, Penetrating
ma_weapons.description: An evolution of a mason's trowel or farmer's tool for digging holes, it is easily concealed by hanging it on the body. It can also be thrown, but is primarily meant as a thrusting weapon or as a makeshift piton.

ma_weapons.name: Mace
ma_weapons.description: Similar to a warhammer, but with a rounded, flanged, or spiked head. Maces are often also badges of office or associated with priestly or ceremonial functions. A morningstar is typically a heavier, spiked mace (piercing) with a longer handle.

ma_weapons.name: Machete
ma_weapons.description: A single edged blade primarily intended as a tool for hacking through crops and underbrush. It may be used as a weapon, but its weight is designed for helping it cleave through obstacles rather than making accurate attacks.

ma_weapons.name: Marbles
ma_weapons.effect: Burst Area Affliction 4 (Resisted by Dodge; Vulnerable, Prone), Continuous, Limited Degree, Limited to Speed 0 or Faster or Fighting
ma_weapons.description: Not designed to cause harm, these stone or glass spheres are dropped upon the ground to make an area precarious to cross. One bag of marbles covers up to a 30- Chapter 8: Tools of the Fight 262 foot radius area. Each time someone moves at a rate greater than Speed -1 (or without sufficient ability to sense the area) through an area containing marbles, or each round someone spends fighting in such an area, the marbles may cause them to trip.

ma_weapons.name: Pistol Grip
ma_weapons.description: A pistol's handgrip may be used as an improvised fist load in a maneuver commonly known as "pistol whipping."

ma_weapons.name: Rifle Butt
ma_weapons.description: The wooden or metal stock of a longarm, such as a rifle or submachine gun, may be used as an improvised club.

ma_weapons.name: Rope
ma_weapons.description: A length of rope with weights or knots tied into it to improve its chance of causing harm. It may also be used to trip an opponent.

ma_weapons.name: Sap
ma_weapons.description: A simple weapon comprised of a bag or the like filled with stones, coins, sand, or something similar. It is used to knock out one's target rather than killing them. Its unassuming nature makes it ideal for street thugs.

ma_weapons.name: Scabbard, Sword
ma_weapons.description: Usually thought as nothing more than something within which to store a blade, a scabbard may be used as a blunt weapon and even thrown short distances. Using a longer scabbard than the blade within also allows small items and powders to be held in the hollow space beyond the blade's tip.

ma_weapons.name: Scythe
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 3 (slashing or piercing), Dangerous 2, Impressive, Inaccurate, Tripping
ma_weapons.description: Originally a tool for cutting wheat and the like, the scythe has since been adapted for use as a two-handed weapon. Its curve is ideal for tripping.

ma_weapons.name: Shovel/Spade
ma_weapons.description: Due to a sharpened edge intended to break ground more easily, a shovel makes a good improvised weapon. Indeed, it has been used as such (to the point of undertaking training with it) by several military forces through the ages.

ma_weapons.name: Sickle, Hand
ma_weapons.description: This weapon is essentially a sickle blade mounted on a short haft the length of a forearm or less. It is meant as a tool for cutting plants.

ma_weapons.name: Tetsubo
ma_weapons.description: The tetsubo or kanabo is a more powerful club shod with iron studs. Legend has them as the weapons of the monstrous oni, and the Japanese saying "like giving a kanabo to an oni" means giving greater advantage to someone who already has an advantage (great strength in the oni's case).

ma_weapons.name: Tonfa
ma_weapons.description: Originally a mill wheel handle, the tonfa is a stick slightly longer than forearm length, with a handle at a right angle, allowing the stick to extend along the wielder's forearm. Tonfa are common close combat weapons for law-enforcement, where they're commonly known as side-handle batons or "T-batons". Archaic Weapons

ma_weapons.name: Axe, Hand
ma_weapons.description: A light, one-handed axe designed for close combat and throwing. A tomahawk or hatchet would also suit this description.

ma_weapons.name: Bagua Saber
ma_weapons.description: A large, curved saber (dao) often used twohanded, this is a ferocious weapon popular during training to improve strength.

ma_weapons.name: Battleaxe
ma_weapons.description: This is a heavy, wide-bladed chopping (slashing) blade attached to a handle.

ma_weapons.name: Dagger/Knife
ma_weapons.description: A short blade, less than 12 inches. Daggers may be single or double edged slashing weapons and are also often usable as piercing weapons. A dagger is typically a Dangerous weapon. Small or folding blades, like a switchblade or butterfly knife, may also be Concealable.

ma_weapons.name: Flail
ma_weapons.description: A handle connected to a heavy (often spiked) weight by a chain or length of strong rope, allowing the weapon's head to swing or spin. A flail grants the benefit of additional Reach.

ma_weapons.name: Greataxe
ma_weapons.description: A big, heavy axe favored by those looking to dole out a lot of damage. It requires both hands to wield properly.

ma_weapons.name: Greatsword
ma_weapons.description: A large, two-handed, wide-bladed sword.

ma_weapons.name: Hunga Munga
ma_weapons.description: Possessing three blades, one of which is considerably curved (for slashing), while the other two are more or less straight (for piercing), this weapon may be used in melee or thrown (use the third Ranged option, pg 258).

ma_weapons.name: Katana
ma_weapons.description: The famous "samurai sword" wielded by noble warriors in feudal Japan. Katanas are slightly curved single-edged blades, worn by samurai with the edge facing up to facilitate Chapter 8: Tools of the Fight 263 quick drawing (the Quick Draw and Iaijitsu advantages are elements of kendo). It is traditionally worn as part of a pair (or daisho) with the shorter wakizashi blade.

ma_weapons.name: Katana, Fantastic
ma_weapons.description: This is a far more cinematic version of the standard katana, and is meant to allow the sort of outrageous combat maneuvers that have made the katana a gaming meme.

ma_weapons.name: Katar
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (piercing or slashing), Penetrating, Reluctant
ma_weapons.description: The Indian "punch dagger" has an H-shaped grip, so the wielder's knuckles rest behind the wide, triangular blade, allowing it to thrust with considerable force, although they can also make slashing attacks. Katar are effective in punching through armor.

ma_weapons.name: Kris
ma_weapons.description: An Indonesian dagger with a distinctive wavy or "flame" blade design, the kris is a cultural icon, and every adult male in Indonesia was expected to own one, often passed down as family heirlooms. The blade design allows kris to inflict terrible wounds. Indonesian legend attributes many supernatural powers to the kris, including the power to kill at a distance simply by pointing at a target, attacking targets by stabbing their shadow or footprints, alerting the wielder to imminent danger, and even controlling fire (flames being similar to the knife's own blade).

ma_weapons.name: Kukri
ma_weapons.description: A heavy Nepalese knife with an inward curving edge, used as both a tool and weapon. Kukri are perhaps most famous for being the favored weapons of Gurkha regiments, including the Royal Gurkha Rifles of the British Army.

ma_weapons.name: Lance
ma_weapons.description: A lance deals its full +3 damage when used from the back of a charging mount. It has reach, so you can strike opponents 10 feet away with it, but you can't use it against a foe nearer than that.

ma_weapons.name: Main-Gauche
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 1 (piercing), Dangerous, Defensive, Disarming, Short Throw
ma_weapons.description: A dagger meant to be wielded in the offhand, it is primarily associated with fencing where it is used to aid in blocking a foe's sword.

ma_weapons.name: Naginata
ma_weapons.description: The Japanese naginata is a wooden haft topped with a curved blade similar to that of a katana or wakizashi. The Chinese guan dao ("reclining moon blade") is a similar weapon with a broader, more cleaver-like blade, traditionally with a red scarf or tassel attached between the blade and shaft. In Japan after the Edo period, the naginata became a symbol of status for women of the samurai class and a common "woman's weapon"--use is still taught to some Japanese schoolgirls as a sport.

ma_weapons.name: Nine-Dragon Trident
ma_weapons.description: A polearm topped with a complex collection of curving and hooked points, particularly effective in blocking and catching enemy weapons and in hooking and tripping opponents, as well as impaling them on one or several of the points.

ma_weapons.name: Ninja-To
ma_weapons.description: A short, straight sword carried and used by ninja. The ninja-to is a single edged blade with a chisel point and a square guard, typically worn in a back sheath and drawn over the shoulder. Many ninjas concealed other weapons upon their ninjato, such as a garrote wrapped around the hilt, extra space at the bottom of the scabbard for hiding things, a hole in the scabbard so it can be used as a snorkel and blowgun, etc. Such additional tricks may be represented by adding Alternate Effects.

ma_weapons.name: No Dachi
ma_weapons.description: This massive, two-handed sword rises well up to the chest on most men and is ideal for attacking armored opponents. It was also used to kill a rider's mount.

ma_weapons.name: Podao
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 3 (slashing or bludgeoning), Double, Reach
ma_weapons.description: A hafted weapon with a broad-headed blade (slashing) on one end and a heavy metal ring (bludgeoning) mounted on the haft's opposite tip.

ma_weapons.name: Rapier
ma_weapons.description: A sword with a long, slender blade primarily intended for thrusting attacks. It is usually fitted with a basket hilt to protect the hand.

ma_weapons.name: Spear
ma_weapons.description: A haft or handle three to six feet long or more, ending in a sharp point. The simplest spears are sharpened sticks (the points often fire hardened). More common are spears with metal heads, often with sharpened Chapter 8: Tools of the Fight 264 edges as well as points, allowing the spear to be swung as a

ma_weapons.name: Sword
ma_weapons.description: Longer blades, over a foot in length, up to four feet or more. Like daggers, swords may be single or double-edged slashing weapons, as well as pointed piercing weapons. Particular sword designs have different qualities, including Binding, Breaking, Dangerous, and Defensive. Enchanted or high-tech swords may have other qualities or powers of their own.

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Claymore
ma_weapons.description: Slightly smaller, lighter, and far more maneuverable than the greatsword. Its size but manageability also makes it useful defensively.

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Falchion
ma_weapons.description: This weapon combines the versatility of a sword with the chopping power of an axe.

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Gladius
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (slashing or piercing), Dangerous, Penetrating
ma_weapons.description: Favored by gladiators and armies that prefer to fight from behind shield walls and the like, this shortsword is intended as a thrusting weapon for piercing armor but also has an edge.

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Wood
ma_weapons.description: Whether known as a bokken, shinai or something else, this is a wooden sword primarily intended for practice, strength training, and the like.

ma_weapons.name: Trident
ma_weapons.description: A spear with three tines or points, it is a piercing weapon. Since the trident is associated with the Greek and Roman sea gods, it is a common weapon and emblem for aquatic characters. Like a spear, a trident can be thrown.

ma_weapons.name: Warhammer
ma_weapons.description: A large hammer with a long haft for enabling a more powerful swing.

ma_weapons.name: Wakizashi
ma_weapons.description: The shorter companion blade to a katana, the wakizashi was primarily useful for close-in fighting (particularly indoors). It was also used for beheading a fallen foe and, most famously, to commit ritual suicide. Exotic Weapons

ma_weapons.name: Chain
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (bludgeoning), Grabbing, Reach 2, Tripping, Weak
ma_weapons.description: A length of chain can strike targets at a distance and can make grabbing and tripping easier.

ma_weapons.name: Chain, Barbed
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (slashing), Dangerous, Grabbing, Reach, Weak
ma_weapons.description: A short length of chain with spikes or barbs tied into the links and attached to a single-grip handle.

ma_weapons.name: Chakar
ma_weapons.description: An unusual weapon wielded by gatka practitioners, a chakar is a flattened wood or metal circle between one and two feet across, spanned by a single rod/handle. Attached at regular intervals along its perimeter are ropes or thin chains ending in weighted balls which are swung into a target by twirling the chakar with both hands using the centralized handle. Using a chakar one-handed is possible but difficult (apply Inaccurate when doing so, but because it is limited to onehanded, the cost cancels out). It may also be thrown, usually high so its spinning weights swing into the target from above.

ma_weapons.name: Kawanga
ma_weapons.description: A oneto three-pronged, light grappling hook attached to a length of rope or thin chain, the kawanga may be used as a raking weapon or to assist in climbing. King Dragon Heart-Piercing Pole/Dragon Pole: A ninefoot staff/pole used by lung ying and wing chun practitioners. It is primarily for building upper body strength, and in training and showmanship more than actual combat.

ma_weapons.name: King Dragon Heart-Piercing Pole/Dragon Pole
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (bludgeoning), Dangerous, Extended, Inaccurate, Reach 2

ma_weapons.name: Kusari-Gama, Blade
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (slashing), Dangerous, Double 19-20 (4) 6 Kusari-Gama, Chain Damage 2 (bludgeoning), Grabbing, Entangling, Reach 20 (5) 6 Latigo Damage 1 (slashing), Grabbing, Reach

ma_weapons.name: Latigo w/Stringray
ma_weapons.effect: Damage 1 (slashing or piercing), Dangerous, Grabbing, Reach

ma_weapons.name: Li Zhao
ma_weapons.description: The "talon gauntlet" is a primary weapon of the si wang long fighting style. It consists of a gauntlet with fingers that have been sharpened to resemble deadly talons, allowing for slashing, claw-like strikes. The talons impose a -2 penalty (skill check or attack, as appropriate) to anything requiring fine use of the fingers, such as operating a computer, tools, or other, hand-held weapons (consider a -1 flat point flaw).

ma_weapons.name: Mancatcher
ma_weapons.description: This weapon consists of a pole with two outwardly curving bands at one end, fitted into a nearly enclosed ring. This ring is pressed around a subject, grabbing them within the bands where spikes press upon them, making any struggling or attempts to yank free the mancatcher from its wielder painful. A mancatcher can also choke an enemy if it ensnares the subject's neck.

ma_weapons.name: Meteor Hammer
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 3 (bludgeoning), Double, Entangling, Reach 2, Tripping
ma_weapons.description: Two heavy spheres are fitted to either end of a chain. The weapon can be swung from the chain, using both spheres to attack simultaneously (Reach 1), or from one of the spheres, extending its reach (Reach 2).

ma_weapons.name: Net
ma_weapons.description: A mesh of strong cord or even metal, thrown or cast over a target to entangle it.

ma_weapons.name: Nunchaku
ma_weapons.description: A pair of sticks or batons (about a foot in length) connected by a short piece of rope or chain, originally an adaptation of a threshing flail. Nunchaku are wielded with circular and twirling motions to deflect incoming attacks and give momentum to the wielder's strikes.

ma_weapons.name: Pata
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (slashing), Easy, Penetrating 2, Reluctant 2, Quirk
ma_weapons.description: This sword is used by wearing the fingerless gauntlet from which its short sword blade extends. Using a pata renders that hand unable to perform any other tasks, as it has no articulate fingers.

ma_weapons.name: Sash Whip
ma_weapons.description: Some Asian cultures used a length of cloth (a belt, sash, or even sarong), often with small weights sewn into it, which could be wielded and cracked like a whip. It is easily camouflaged as a mundane garment when not in use.

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Chain
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (slashing), Grabbing, Inaccurate, Reach, Uncertain
ma_weapons.description: This weapon is comprised of two sword blades, each over a foot long, connected by a length of chain. An awkward weapon to use, it is easily concealed and the blades may be disconnected for throwing.

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Hook
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 3 (slashing), Double or Reach, Tripping
ma_weapons.description: These Chinese weapons, usually wielded in pairs, are designed with curved hooks at the end of the blade, a crescent-shaped handguard, and a sharp, daggerlike pommel. This design allows the swords to be wielded in a variety of ways. Hook swords are effective at tripping, catching opposing weapons, and blocking. They can even be hooked together at the tips, swinging the second sword out so its pommel slashes, extending the wielder's reach (+1 Reach while doing so).

ma_weapons.name: Sword, Khopesh
ma_weapons.description: This large blade has a hook at the end. It is particularly useful for making trip attacks or smashing objects.

ma_weapons.name: Three-Section-Staff
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 2 (bludgeoning), Disarming, Double, Impressive, Reach
ma_weapons.description: This weapon is used in a similar fashion as nunchaku, but has three segments. It can be used as a double weapon with greater reach.

ma_weapons.name: Urumi
ma_weapons.description: This coiling sword has a single flexible, whiplike blade. Experts can move it to whip and mold around their body, lashing out to cut or grasp an opponent. The difficulty of correctly using this blade can make it dangerous to its wielder, as well.

ma_weapons.name: Velayudaya
ma_weapons.effect: Damage 2 (slashing), Dangerous, Disarming, Grabbing, Reach, Risky, Uncertain 3
ma_weapons.description: This whip-like weapon is fitted with four lengths of flexible metal, each of which sports a double edge. The metal strips are capable of cutting and flaying an opponent (or an inexperienced wielder) with surprising lethality. This weapon is used by masters of angampora.

ma_weapons.name: War Fan *
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 1 (bludgeoning or slashing), Concealed, Defensive

ma_weapons.name: Whip
ma_weapons.description: A long, flexible strand, often braided leather, a whip can be cracked so the tip strikes with considerable force, used as a goad for animals (or even sentient slaves or prisoners). A whip can also wrap around a limb or limbs to restrain a target.

ma_weapons.name: Whip, Chain
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Damage 1 (bludgeoning), Concealable, Grabbing, Reach 2, Weak
ma_weapons.description: A series of metal bars held together by chain links, this weapon can be folded up and hidden within one's clothes to be unleashed and swung when needed. Each end is fitted with a weight that can deliver a lashing strike, aids in building momentum, and/or may be caught so that the weapon may change hands.

ma_weapons.name: Yo-Yo
ma_weapons.effect: Damage 1 (bludgeoning or slashing if sharpened), Concealable, Reach
ma_weapons.description: Traditionally a toy with a length of string wrapped around an axle/spool fixed between two disks, practitioners of yo-yodo have turned it into a weapon. Using momentum and gravity, the disks are unspooled at the target before bringing the yo-yo back by pulling on the string, winding it back around the spool. The disks of some combat yo-yos are of sharpened or even serrated metal rather than wood or plastic. Ranged Weapons The following ranged weapons use the first option for ranged weapons presented earlier in this work (pg 258). Many of the previous weapons--particularly some blades and polearms-- can also be thrown using the second or third options for ranged weapons.

ma_weapons.name: Arrow: Broad Head
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Damage as bow +2 ranks, Ammunition, Inaccurate

ma_weapons.name: Arrow: Dragon's Tongue
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Damage as bow, Ammunition, Penetrating

ma_weapons.name: Arrow: Fish Point
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Damage as bow, Ammunition, Secondary Effect, Triggered

ma_weapons.name: Arrow: Frog Crotch
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Damage as bow, Ammunition, Smashing (limited to cutting)

ma_weapons.name: Arrow: Skinsplitter
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Damage as bow, Ammunition, Dangerous

ma_weapons.name: Arrow: Willow Leaf
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Damage as bow, Ammunition, Precise

ma_weapons.name: Blowgun
ma_weapons.effect: Ranged Affliction (Poison; Resisted and Overcome by Fortitude; Impaired, Disabled, Incapacitated; Resistible [Toughness])
ma_weapons.description: A hollow tube used to fire small darts by blowing into one end. The blowgun is typically a weapon for hunting or assassination using darts tipped with poisons because the weapon's actual damage is negligible.

ma_weapons.name: Bow
ma_weapons.description: Whether an archaic weapon of wood (often reinforced with horn or similar materials) or a modern bow made of metal or composites, it fires bladed or pointed arrows. A wide range of "trick" arrows are common (see the Trick Arrows section, pg 268) Some bows are specially crafted to work with the wielder's strength. This allows the bow's Damage to become Strength-Based. The Gamemaster should appropriately increase the value and DC to create such weapons compared to standard bows. Chapter 8: Tools of the Fight 268

ma_weapons.name: Crossbow
ma_weapons.description: Like a bow, but with a pistol-like trigger and stock, and generally easier to load and draw. A modern crossbow might even be semi-automatic, self-loading with each pull of the trigger.

ma_weapons.name: Daikyu
ma_weapons.effect: Strength-Based Ranged Damage 4 (piercing), Dangerous, Extended Range
ma_weapons.description: An incredibly long bow standing taller than most men, the Japanese longbow is traditionally made of bamboo and fitted with a hemp string to grant it impressive power. Daikyu add the wielder's Strength bonus to their damage.

ma_weapons.name: Hankyu
ma_weapons.description: A short bow designed to be easily concealed and non-encumbering, the bow, therefore, suffers from a lack of power. Hankyu add some of the wielder's Strength bonus to their damage. There is a variation that collapses, making it and its arrows easier to hide. Add the Concealable quality (+1 point) to such a version.

ma_weapons.name: Sling
ma_weapons.description: A small pouch able to hold a stone or metal "bullet" sphere. It is typically spun from cords, and one end of the weapon is released to sling the stone at the target. Staff slings place the pouch at the end of a long handle, which is swung or snapped to fire the sling bullet.

ma_weapons.name: Slingshot
ma_weapons.description: A small, hand-held ranged weapon that uses an elastic sling mounted between two forks to propel a small stone, metal ball, or the like. Technically a child's toy, a slingshot can be surprisingly effective and accurate although its range is incredibly limited. Most modern slingshots collapse for ease of concealment and storage. ma_weapons.name: Bolos
ma_weapons.description: This is a set of three or four weights connected by cords to a central hub. A bolo is thrown in such a way as to make the weights spin around the center point, allowing the cords to wrap around the target and restrain it. Like other thrown weapons, bolos use one of the three options listed for ranged weapons (pg 258).

ma_weapons.name: Boomerang
ma_weapons.description: A common throwing weapon for heroes, a thrown boomerang returns to the thrower's hand, ready to be thrown again in the next round (less a Feature and more a special descriptor). Boomerang wielders often use this property of the weapon to feint, allowing for an attack against a vulnerable target on the return arc on the attacker's next turn.

ma_weapons.name: Chakram
ma_weapons.description: This Indian throwing weapon is a metal ring with a sharpened outer edge, spun when it is thrown for additional cutting power. A master chakram wielder may have the Throwing Mastery advantage and the Ricochet extra as a power with the training or skill descriptors.

ma_weapons.name: Dart
ma_weapons.description: A weighted throwing spike, typically with vanes or fletching to help guide its flight.

ma_weapons.name: Javelin
ma_weapons.description: A thin, light spear about three feet long, primarily designed for throwing.

ma_weapons.name: Nageteppo: Flash Powder
ma_weapons.effect: Burst Area Affliction 3 (Resisted and Overcome by Fortitude; Impaired, Disabled, Unaware), Limited to Sight

ma_weapons.name: Nageteppo: Lacquer Poison
ma_weapons.effect: Cloud Area Affliction 3 (Resisted and Overcome by Fortitude; Impaired, Disabled), Limited Degree

ma_weapons.name: Shuriken
ma_weapons.description: These Japanese throwing weapons come in two main types: spike or bo shuriken are short metal spikes similar to large nails while star shuriken are flat star-shaped wheels with sharpened edges. Both are relatively easily concealed in sleeves or sashes and typically thrown several at a time (giving them the Multiattack modifier). Ninjas are infamous for applying poisons to the points and edges of shuriken, adding an Affliction effect (resisted and overcome by Fortitude) to the weapon's damage.

ma_weapons.name: Steel Ball
ma_weapons.description: This is essentially an over-sized ball bearing used for throwing. It has the advantage of not appearing as a weapon and being easy to conceal. If desperate, it can also be wrapped in a cloth or the like and used as a close ranged weapon with the Inaccurate quality. Trick Arrows The following arrowheads can be manufactured by anyone with sufficient talent, but are mainly used by characters that will employ the bow (or crossbow) as the primary expression of their abilities. Each arrow is presented in terms of its cost per rank, allowing the Gamemaster and players to customize them as desired, or as a flat cost, as appropriate. The cost of the Ammunition extra assumes +0, but increase to +1 cost per rank if the trick arrow's range would

ma_weapons.name: Helicopter Blade
ma_weapons.description: When torn from a helicopter's main rotor, one of these blades can serve as an impromptu sword.

ma_weapons.name: I-Beam
ma_weapons.description: Typical of the sort found on a high-rise construction site, this steel beam is intended to act as a structure's supporting skeleton but can make an effective club.

ma_weapons.name: Manhole Cover
ma_weapons.description: A round, metal plate used to cover a street's manhole. Although they are useful for hitting an opponent with, they can also be used as shields. Manhole covers can be thrown, although doing so deprives the wielder of the weapon.

ma_weapons.name: Parking Meter
ma_weapons.description: The old fashioned, "Insert coin, spin knob" variety that may be rooted up from the ground and swung like a club by its steel pole.

ma_weapons.name: Power Line
ma_weapons.effect: Damage 2 (slashing), Disarming, Grabbing, Reach 2+, Tripping, Weak
ma_weapons.description: These high-tension cables are ideal for dishing out a good lashing, with weight and length varying (increase Extended Reach to suit longer sections). These statistics may also be used for telephone wire, although the Toughness is reduced to 5. Determine a powerline's weight based on its length (and thus its reach): 15 lbs per 5 feet.

ma_weapons.name: Street Light
ma_weapons.description: Whether torn directly from the ground or picked up after being knocked down during a fight, street lights or lamp posts can make for handy improvised clubs.

ma_weapons.name: Tank Turret
ma_weapons.description: When torn off the tank's chassis, the main turret may be grasped by the cannon and swung like an oddly weighted club. ma_weapons.description: A much heavier version of the small wrecking ball, this demolition tool is usually used against reinforced structures. Armor

ma_armor.name: Fencing
ma_armor.description: A full suit made of durable nylon or cotton, ballistic material has been added to the upper suit. The face mask is comprised of a plastic or metal mesh screen over and around the face (some competitions now allow for a plastic viewing plate amongst the mesh) with a bib hanging beneath to protect the neck. The suit only protects against piercing attacks.

ma_armor.name: Kendo
ma_armor.description: Comprised of a helmet sporting a metal grill to protect the face, a wooden breastplate covers the chest while three padded, fabric faulds cover the waist's front. Fabric gauntlets with thick padding protect the forearms, wrists, and hands.

ma_armor.name: Samurai
ma_armor.description: Largely formed from layers of protective "scale" plates of metal where the body was most vulnerable and leather strips and scales elsewhere. The helmet typically sported a stylized face plate.

ma_armor.name: Sparring
ma_armor.effect: Protection 2, Quirk (Hand and Foot Attacks become Nonlethal)
ma_armor.description: Used during practice bouts and competitions, this "armor" is little more than padding to cover the hands, top of the feet, and head (although the face remains exposed). Aside from providing protection, it also reduces the chance of harming one's opponents.

ma_armor.name: Stealth Suit
ma_armor.effect: Protection 2; Concealment 2 (Infravision), Partial, Passive; Enhanced Stealth 2 (+4)
ma_armor.description: Used by high-tech espionage infiltrators and assassins, the suit is designed to blend into shadows and the like. Also, its materials muffle the sounds of movement and cool the body, reducing the wearer's heat signature.

ma_armor.name: Training Armor
ma_armor.effect: Impervious Protection 3, Limited to Bludgeoning, Reduced Agility 1 *
ma_armor.description: This modern protective suit consists of heavily padded, open-faced headgear, chest protector, and shin guards. Some also come with padding for the top of the feet, adding Quirk (Foot Attacks become Nonlethal). The pads are not designed to protect against real weapons. Mystic and Outlandish Martial Arts Equipment The following weapons and items are designed as examples of the sort of mystical and unusual type of gear one would expect to find in the hands of someone who combines oriental mysticism or otherworldly skill with their martial arts. Some are a general type of weapon or item while others

trick_arrows.name: Acid Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Weaken Toughness, Affects Objects, Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead breaks, splashing an acid around the point of impact that eats through organic and inorganic matter. Add the Area extra to expand the arrow's splash.

trick_arrows.name: Adhesive Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Dodge, Overcome by Strength and Damage; Hindered and Vulnerable, Defenseless and Immobile), Ammunition, Contagious, Extra Condition, Limited Degree
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead makes whatever it strikes sticky with a special adhesive. This will not only stick the target to a nearby surface (what depends on where the target is struck), but also makes anything subsequently touching that spot also stick to it. Add the Area extra to expand the arrow's effect.

trick_arrows.name: Armor Piercing Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Penetrating
trick_arrows.description: Regardless of the arrow's other aspects, it is also intended to punch through armor.

trick_arrows.name: Blunted Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage, Ammunition, Nonlethal
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead has no point and is sufficiently cushioned that it does not deliver a lethal blow. Chapter 8: Tools of the Fight

trick_arrows.name: Boomerang Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage, Ammunition, Indirect
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead releases two spring-loaded wings while in flight, allowing it to bypass the intended target, boomerang, and strike from behind on the arrow's return course.

trick_arrows.name: Bouncing Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage, Ammunition, Ricochet
trick_arrows.description: The arrow is designed to be bounced off an appropriate surface to strike at an intended target following the ricochet without it losing any of its edge or momentum. Add more ranks of Ricochet to allow the arrow to bounce more than once.

trick_arrows.name: Climbing Line Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Movement 1 (Wall-Crawling), Ammunition, Limited to Wall-Crawling towards Target Point
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead unspools a light line behind it, allowing someone to then climb up the line between the arrow's point of original and wherever it strikes.

trick_arrows.name: Concussive Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage, Ammunition, Enhanced Knockback*, Knockback Only
trick_arrows.description: The arrow releases a contained concussive explosion upon impact. This is pure force that is intended to be nonlethal. Add more ranks of Enhanced Knockback to make the arrowhead more potent, and an Area to make the concussive blast larger. * See Better Mousetrap 3e Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Effect: Ranged Weaken Electronics, Affects Only Objects, Broad, Simultaneous, Ammunition 4 points per rank The arrow emits a powerful-but-focused electromagnetic pulse (EMP) on impact that overloads electronics in the target. Weakened electronics must be repaired or components replaced to recover from its effects. Add the Area extra to spread this effect over a wider area.

trick_arrows.name: Explosive Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Burst Area Ranged Damage, Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: per rank An explosion is detonated upon the arrow's impact. Increase the ranks of Burst Area to increase the explosion's size.

trick_arrows.name: Fire-Fighting Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Burst Area Nullify Fire, Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: A burst of fire-fighting foam is unleashed upon impact. Increase the ranks of Burst Area to increase the amount of area covered in foam.

trick_arrows.name: Flare Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Environmental Control (Light, 2 points/rank), Ammunition, Liberated *
trick_arrows.description: The arrow unleashes a phosphorous glow at the apex of its flight or upon impact, filling the area with light. Add more ranks of Liberated to make the flare's light last longer. * See Better Mousetrap 3e

trick_arrows.name: Flash Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Cumulative Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Fortitude; Impaired, Disabled, Unaware), Ammunition, Limited to Vision
trick_arrows.description: The arrow unleashes a bright-but-localized, blinding flash upon impact. Add the Burst Area extra if you'd like the flash to blind over a greater area.

trick_arrows.name: Flash-Bang Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Cumulative Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Will; Impaired, Disabled, Unaware), Ammunition, Extra Condition (Sense), Limited to Auditory and Vision
trick_arrows.description: On impact, the arrowhead bursts loudly and with a blinding light. Add the Burst Area extra if you'd like the flash-bang to blind and deafen over a greater area.

trick_arrows.name: Freezing Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage (Cold), Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead releases a freezing agent over the point of impact. Add an Area if you want the freezing cold to spread around more. Tear gas is both sickeningly choking and blinding.

trick_arrows.name: Incendiary Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage (Fire), Ammunition, Contagious
trick_arrows.description: The arrow sparks with ignited white phosphorous on impact, not only burning the point of impact but potentially also starting a fire.

trick_arrows.name: Microphone Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Communication 2 (Radio), Ammunition, Subtle, Limited to Broadcasting
trick_arrows.description: When the arrow hits its target, a microphone in the arrowhead is activated. The microphone then broadcasts what it hears nearby.

trick_arrows.name: Net Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Burst Area Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Dodge, Overcome by Strength and Damage; Hindered and Vulnerable, Defenseless and Immobile), Ammunition, Extra Condition, Limited Degree
trick_arrows.description: On impact, the entire arrow breaks apart, unfurling a net over the target area.

trick_arrows.name: Riot Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Burst Area Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Fortitude; Dazed, Stunned, Incapacitated), Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: per rank On impact, the arrowhead unleashes a barrage of rubber pellets, tiny bean bags, an electrical shock, or something similar that fills the area with a crowd control effect.

trick_arrows.name: Screamer Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Cumulative Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Fortitude; Impaired, Disabled, Unaware), Ammunition, Limited to Auditory
trick_arrows.description: The arrow unleashes a loud-but-localized, deafening screech upon impact. Add the Burst Area extra if you'd like the sound to deafen over a greater area. Alternatively or additionally, apply sufficient ranks of the Line Area with Alternate Attack (Ranged) * and remove the Ranged extra to have the screamer unleash its sound along its flight trajectory. * See Better Mousetrap 3e

trick_arrows.name: Shocking Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Damage (Electricity), Ammunition, Contagious
trick_arrows.description: This arrowhead zaps its target with a powerful electrical shock upon impact. The electricity may travel through conductive materials. Add the Burst Area if you want the electricity to discharge over a wider area.

trick_arrows.name: Shotgun Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Cone Area Ranged Damage, Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: per rank On impact, the arrowhead fires a cone of buckshot in the direction it is facing, much like a shotgun.

trick_arrows.name: Slick Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Burst Area Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Dodge, Overcome by Agility/Acrobatics; Vulnerable and Prone), Ammunition, Limited Degree 2
trick_arrows.description: Chapter 8: Tools of the Fight Optional Rule: Improvised Weapon Damage If you want improvised weapons to stand apart from standard weapons a bit more, try the following option rule when it comes to their Damage modifier. The Damage modifier of an improvised weapon is equal to the wielder's Strength instead of that which is provided here. If the weapon's Toughness exceeds the wielder's Strength, there is an additional Damage bonus applied equal to the difference between the two, up to +2. A character with Strength 8 is wielding a tank turret as an improvised weapon. The tank would normally be Damage 5, but its Toughness of 12 is higher than the character's Strength by 4, so this applies an additional bonus of +2 (the maximum possible). In this character's hands, the tank turret is a Close Damage 10 weapon. On impact, the arrowhead covers the immediate area with an incredibly slippery substance.

trick_arrows.name: Smoke Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Cloud Area Ranged Concealment 2 (Visual), Ammunition, Attack, Liberated *
trick_arrows.description: On impact, the arrowhead mixes chemicals that create a thick cloud of smoke around it. * See Better Mousetrap 3e

trick_arrows.name: Tangle Line Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Dodge, Overcome by Damage/Strength; Prone and Vulnerable, Defenseless and Immobilized), Ammunition, Extra Condition, Limited Degree
trick_arrows.description: On impact, this blunted arrowhead unleashes a cord with weighted ends. The cord's weights use the arrow's momentum to wrap around the target, possibly tripping and ensnaring it.

trick_arrows.name: Taser Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Range Affliction (Resisted by Fortitude; Dazed, Stunned, Incapacitated), Ammunition, Contagious
trick_arrows.description: Being struck by this arrow means being zapped with a powerful electrical discharge intended to stun rather than cause actual harm. The electrical charge may travel through conductive materials.

trick_arrows.name: Tracer Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Senses 2 (Direction Sense, Distance Sense), Ammunition, Limited to Relative to Arrow's Position
trick_arrows.description: Activated when the arrow strikes something, the arrowhead contains a tracer beacon that someone who knows the signal's frequency may use to follow to the arrowhead's location.

trick_arrows.name: Tranquilizer Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Affliction (Resisted by Fortitude; Dazed, Stunned, Incapacitated), Ammunition, Sleep
trick_arrows.description: per rank The arrowhead injects its target with a tranquilizer upon impact, making the subject groggy or possibly putting them to sleep.

trick_arrows.name: Whistle Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Ranged Feature (Whistle), Ammunition
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead has holes placed within it that allows air to pass through during flight, resulting in a loud whistle so long as the arrow remains airborne. This may be added to other trick arrow types to create a whistling variation.

trick_arrows.name: White Noise Arrow
trick_arrows.effect: Burst Area Ranged Concealment (Auditory), Ammunition, Attack, Liberated *
trick_arrows.description: The arrowhead emits white noise on impact, effectively canceling any other sound in the area. * See Better Mousetrap 3e

mystic_items.name: Bracers of the Monkey
mystic_items.description: Rumored to have been created by Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, these bracers grant the wearer understanding and ability with the monkey fist fighting style so long as they are worn. The Monkey King is not without a sense of humor, however. The wearer has been known to initiate hou quan maneuvers when least expected--crawling up walls when intending to only step out of someone's way, for instance, or uttering "ook, ook" or otherwise acting distinctly monkey-like in the middle of a conversation. Bracers of the Monkey (Removable): Variable 4 (Any Hou Quan Trait), Limited to Hou Quan Traits Not Already Known, Quirk (Monkey-Like Behavior), Uncontrolled - 15 points

mystic_items.name: Artifact of the Way
mystic_items.cost_text: 5 points per rank plus Removable or Easily Removable
mystic_items.description: These items, which range in appearance from a flashy piece of jewelry to a nondescript sash, have each been empowered by a master of both sorcery and the martial arts. They grant the wielder enhanced or entirely new martial talents, although what manifests is not within the wielder's control. Although fate usually gives them what they need (well, as best as the relevant fighting style is able to), it frequently acts to bestow the artifact's "gifts" at inopportune moments. Artifact of the Way (Removable): Variable (Any Trait of Respective Fighting Style), Limited to Fighting Style Traits Not Already Known, Uncontrolled - 5 points per rank plus Removable or Easily Removable Gamemasters should

mystic_items.name: Blade of the Celestial Emperor
mystic_items.description: Thought to have purposefully been left on Earth by the Celestial Emperor of the Taoist faith--to what ends no one knows--this blade grants the wielder unimagined power. Legend holds that the blade was hidden by monks so only someone worthy of its power could find the clues scattered around the world, requiring a great quest be undertaken to find it. Blade of the Celestial Emperor (Easily Removable): Strength-Based Damage 4, Accurate, Combo Element, Multiattack, Penetrating 4; Enhanced Strength 5; Enhanced Stamina 5; Enhanced Agility 5; Enhanced Fighting 5; Variable 2 (Enhance Fighting Style Traits), Limited to Possessed Fighting Style Skills, Advantages, and Basic and Advanced Combat Maneuve

mystic_items.name: Daikyu of Shooting Stars
mystic_items.description: This enchanted bow is believed to have been crafted by the gods. It can fire incomparable distances with high accuracy. Daikyu of Shooting Stars (Easily Removable): Strength-Based Ranged Damage 5, Improved Critical 2, Extended Range 10; Enhanced Ranged Combat: Daikyu 6, Limited to Canceling Range Penalties - 15 points

mystic_items.name: Dragon Sword
mystic_items.description: Not truly magical, these rarest of katana are the work of the best swordmasters ancient Japan had to offer. The knowledge of how to create such durable, deadly, and priceless blades has since become lost in the darkness of history, unfortunately. Even today's most technologically apt craftsmen have been unable to replicate the techniques used to forge these invaluable blades. Dragon Sword (Easily Removable): Strength-Based Damage 6, Improved Critical 4, Penetrating 6 - 10 points Fiery Weapon Plus 18 points A fiery weapon (typically a sword) is one that has been enchanted to burst into flame. This is a common weapon in martial arts stories. Fiery Weapon: Strike 3 (Fire), Reaction (Contact), S

mystic_items.name: Scorpion's Lash
mystic_items.description: This is an unusual, extremely unorthodox weapon utilized by du zhua quan practitioners (pg 229). It consists of a thin chain with a sharpened, spike-like barb (the "scorpion's stinger") several inches long and weighted towards one end. The other end extends from the palm, through a metal ring fastened there by a special glove that stretches all the way down to the elbow. A spring-loaded device near the elbow causes the chain's length to pull around the forearm, guided by metal loops sewn to the gauntlet. A powerful, sharp flick of the arm causes the chain to unspool, lashing out to its full length, only to be pulled back immediately afterward. Scorpion's Lash: Affliction 5 (Resisted by Dodge
